rv.q: The musical Cagney, which opened last night at the Westside Theater, is a thoroughly entertaining evening of song and dance served by an outstanding ensemble of performers, who can do it all with consummate flair.
If you like musical theater, film history and James Cagney, this is the show for you.
Cagney may be imperfect, but this low-concept, high-energy show has so much going for it under the direction of Bill Castellino...

This show is so full of vitality, swirling feet, crowd-pleasing songs and dances that you have to look at your Playbill to believe so many characters filling the stage are played by a supporting cast of only five people.
CAGNEY's return to Off-Broadway, with the same cast, director and choreographer, is a slicker, fuller production that should send Westside Theatre audiences out with big smiles.
But as I say, Creighton as Cagney just kills it.
Its good-natured tone and Robert Creighton’s colossal performance make Cagney satisfying entertainment especially for those familiar with the movie legend.
Creighton and company will give you an evening you won’t soon forget.
Cagney is not to be missed and you will be humming those songs as you leave the theater!
When you follow Robert Creighton down the rabbit hole you end up in a wonderland that you can feel down to your toes.
This musical is a joyous tribute to a talented New Yorker whose fancy footwork and captivating stage presence carved an indelible niche for himself in Hollywood, whether toting a gun or tap shoes.
You’ll be giving your regards to Broadway and on your feet, applauding.
This James Cagney bio-musical is fizzy fun with just enough seriousness to make it a satisfying tribute to the pugnacious movie star.
Fortunately, in addition to singing, dancing, and tapping a mean streak, Creighton bears a striking physical resemblance to Cagney.
Cagney is a bonafide crowd pleaser and although this cast is working earnestly for their paychecks, they are doing it in such an effortless manner with good ‘ole Yankee Doodle flair.
For a good old fashion enjoyable time Cagney is a Yankee Doodle Dandy.
He’s an excellent Cagney, and when he gets to dance, replicating the star’s uncanny melt-away and pop-up style – like that of a decoy duck with elastic legs – he’s a phenomenon.
What’s missing in this musical interpretation of Cagney’s life is that incomparable bit of spark that made James Cagney so singular and exceptional.
In its present form, “Cagney” is highly entertaining and well worth a trip to the iconic Westside Theatre.
Knowing this, director Bill Castellino keeps things flowing so quickly that it’s impossible not to get drawn into the fun.
The rousing musical is full of song and tap dance which will excite audiences of all ages.

cn.t: Critics praise Robert Creighton's dynamic, charismatic performance as Cagney and the show's energetic tap dancing, calling it entertaining and spirited.
